chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Spasm bands, the ukulele craze and grandfather's coach driving
summary: Danny saw kids earning money in spasm bands, while his grandfather played funerals and drove coaches until limousines replaced horses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So, in the (?) the ukelele craze had come out. So I'd see these little kids around in their little spasm bands in the French Quarter makin' money, the White Folks throwing [t'rowin] them money -- and I see that everybody was makin' some money with this music business. My grandfather, he's supplementing the money. He's playing like maybe two funerals a week, sometimes three, and he's working as a coach driver... It put him out of business when they changed from horses to limousines; it throwed him out the whole business altogether.
My grandfather was a hackman in Vicksburg, too -- my mother's father.
Yeah. So that was quite a... It was a good profession.
Yeah. That was a high-class gig.
Yeah. Because you had to be careful with them people, you had to have responsible horses in order to let them ride comfortably, and be careful how you drove.
